# Question 1

```{r}
# spatial data science
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(units)

# Data
library(AOI)

# Visualization
library(gghighlight)
library(ggrepel)
library(knitr)
```

```{r}
eqdc <- '+proj=eqdc +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs'
```

```{r}
# Get USA continental state boundaries
conus_states <- aoi_get(state = 'conus')

# Reproject to eqdc
conus_states_eqdc <- st_transform(conus_states, crs = eqdc)
```

```{r}
# Get country boundaries
countries <- aoi_get(country = c("MX", "CA", "USA"))

# Reproject
countries_eqdc <- st_transform(countries, crs = eqdc)
```

```{r}
library(readr)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# Read CSV
cities_raw <- read_csv("data/uscities.csv")

# Step 3: Convert the cities data to a spatial object (assuming lat/lon in WGS84)
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_raw, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# Step 4: Reproject to the desired coordinate system (eqdc)
eqdc <- '+proj=eqdc +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs'
cities_eqdc <- st_transform(cities_sf, crs = eqdc)

# Step 5: Filter out CONUS states by state abbreviation
conus_state_names <- conus_states$state_abbr  # Get state abbreviations from CONUS states

# Step 6: Convert the spatial object to a data frame for easier manipulation
cities_eqdc_df <- as.data.frame(cities_eqdc)

# Step 7: Inspect the state_id column to ensure it’s a character vector
# (This is just for troubleshooting and should not be necessary if the column is correct)
str(cities_eqdc_df$state_id)  # Check if it's a list or a character vector

# Step 8: If state_id is a list, flatten it into a character vector
cities_eqdc_df$state_id <- unlist(cities_eqdc_df$state_id)

# Step 9: Now filter the cities by CONUS state abbreviations
cities_eqdc_conus <- cities_eqdc_df %>%
  filter(state_id %in% conus_state_names)

# Step 10: Convert back to an sf object using the geometry column (no need to specify coords)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_eqdc_conus)

# Check the result
head(cities_eqdc_conus_sf)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Ensure cities_eqdc_conus is an sf object with geometry
cities_eqdc_conus_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_eqdc_conus)

# Check the structure to ensure it has the geometry column
str(cities_eqdc_conus_sf)

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = countries_eqdc, fill = "gray90") +
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_eqdc, fill = "white", color = "black") +
  geom_sf(data = cities_eqdc_conus_sf, color = "red", size = 0.5) +  # Ensure correct data object with geometry
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(eqdc)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Question 2

```{r}
# Combine all state geometries into one unified geometry
usa_border <- conus_states_eqdc %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")  # Ensure it's a MULTILINESTRING for distance calculations

# Check the result
plot(usa_border)
```

```{r}
# Calculate the distance from each city to the nearest national border (USA)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_border <- st_distance(cities_eqdc_conus_sf, usa_border)

# Convert to kilometers (default is meters)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_border_km <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_border / 1000
```

```{r}
# Sort cities by distance to the border (in km) and select top 5
top_5_farthest_cities <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  arrange(desc(distance_to_border_km)) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  select(city, state_name, distance_to_border_km)

# Create a flextable to display the results
library(flextable)
top_5_farthest_cities_ft <- flextable(top_5_farthest_cities)

# Print the flextable
top_5_farthest_cities_ft
```

```{r}
# Convert each state's boundary into MULTILINESTRING geometry
state_borders <- conus_states_eqdc %>%
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING")  # Preserve individual state borders
```

```{r}
# Calculate the distance from each city to the nearest state border (USA state boundary)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_state_border <- st_distance(cities_eqdc_conus_sf, state_borders)

# Convert distance to kilometers (default is in meters)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_state_border_km <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf$distance_to_state_border / 1000
```

```{r}
# Extract the minimum distance for each city (convert to km)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  mutate(distance_to_state_border_km = apply(distance_to_state_border_km, 1, function(x) min(x) / 1000))  # Convert from meters to km

# Now, sort by distance and select the top 5
top_5_farthest_state_borders <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  arrange(desc(distance_to_state_border_km)) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  select(city, state_name, distance_to_state_border_km)

# Create a flextable to display the results
library(flextable)
top_5_farthest_state_borders_ft <- flextable(top_5_farthest_state_borders)

# Print the flextable
top_5_farthest_state_borders_ft
```
```{r}

  mutate(distance_to_mexico_border_km = st_distance(geometry, mexico_border) / 1000)  # Convert from meters to km

# Step 3: Sort by distance and select the top 5 cities farthest from Mexico

top_5_farthest_mexico_borders_ft
```

# Question 3

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(dplyr)

# Step 1: Load and prepare your data (if needed)
# Assuming cities_eqdc_conus_sf and conus_states_eqdc are already available

# Step 2: Get the top 10 largest cities by population
top_10_cities <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  head(10)

# Step 3: Plot the map using ggplot
ggplot() +
  # Add continents layer
  geom_sf(data = countries_eqdc, fill = "gray90", color = "black", lwd = 0.5) +
  
  # Add CONUS boundary layer (the United States)
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_eqdc, fill = "white", color = "black", lwd = 0.8, lty = 1) +
  
  # Add state boundaries
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_eqdc, fill = NA, color = "black", lwd = 0.5, lty = 2) +
  
  # Add the 10 largest cities, with labels
  geom_sf(data = top_10_cities, aes(geometry = geometry), color = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_label_repel(data = top_10_cities, aes(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], 
                                              y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2], 
                                              label = city), 
                   size = 3, 
                   box.padding = 0.35, 
                   max.overlaps = 10, 
                   nudge_y = 0.1) +
  
  # Add title and theme
  labs(title = "Top 10 Largest U.S. Cities (by Population) with State Boundaries",
       subtitle = "Showing the 3 Continents, CONUS Outline, State Boundaries, and City Labels") +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(dplyr)

# Step 1: Assuming cities_eqdc_conus_sf contains the distance to national border in the 'distance_to_national_border_km' column
# and cities_eqdc_conus_sf is an sf object containing city geometries.

# Step 2: Sort and select the 5 cities farthest from the national border
top_5_farthest_from_border <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  arrange(desc(distance_to_border_km)) %>%  # Sort by distance to national border
  head(5) %>%  # Select the top 5 cities
  select(city, state_name, distance_to_border_km)

top_5_farthest_from_border

# Step 3: Plot the map
ggplot() +

   geom_sf(data = conus_states_eqdc, fill = "white", color = "black", lwd = 0.8) +

        subtitle = "Top 5 Cities Farthest from the National Border Labeled") +

   theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)

# Step 1: Convert the distance columns to numeric values (in km)
cities_eqdc_conus_sf <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  mutate(
    distance_to_mexico_border_km = as.numeric(distance_to_mexico_border_km), 
    distance_to_canada_border_km = as.numeric(distance_to_canada_border_km)
  )

# Step 2: Create a new variable for the absolute difference between the distance to Mexico and Canada
cities_eqdc_conus_sf <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  mutate(distance_difference = abs(distance_to_mexico_border_km - distance_to_canada_border_km))

# Step 3: Filter cities that are roughly equidistant from both borders (100 km) and have minimal difference
equidistant_cities <- cities_eqdc_conus_sf %>%
  filter(
    distance_to_mexico_border_km <= 100, 
    distance_to_canada_border_km <= 100,
    distance_difference <= 10  # Threshold for "equidistant"
  )

# Step 4: Sort and select the 5 most populous cities in the equidistant zone
top_5_populous_in_zone <- equidistant_cities %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  select(city, state_name, population, distance_to_mexico_border_km, distance_to_canada_border_km)

# Step 5: Plot with improved color visualization
ggplot() +
  # Add CONUS boundary (states)
  geom_sf(data = conus_states_eqdc, fill = "white", color = "black", lwd = 0.8) +
  
  # Plot equidistant cities with color gradient for distance difference
  geom_sf(data = equidistant_cities, 
          aes(color = distance_difference), 
          size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Label the top 5 most populous cities in the equidistant zone
  geom_label_repel(data = top_5_populous_in_zone, 
                   aes(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], 
                       y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2], 
                       label = city), 
                   size = 3, 
                   box.padding = 0.3, 
                   nudge_y = 0.1, 
                   max.overlaps = 10) +
  
  # Use the viridis color scale
  scale_color_viridis(
    option = "magma", 
    direction = -1, 
    name = "Distance Difference (km)"
  ) +
  
  # Add title and theme
  labs(title = "Cities Equidistant from Mexico and Canada (within 100 km)",
       subtitle = "Top 5 Most Populous Cities Labeled") +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
# Question 4

```{r}
library(knitr)

border_table <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Number of cities in the 100-mile zone",
    "Population within the 100-mile zone",
    "Percentage of U.S. population in this zone",
    "Matches ACLU estimate?"
  ),
  Estimate = c(
    "Over 2,000 incorporated cities",
    "Approximately 200 million people",
    "About 60–66% (2 out of 3 Americans)",
    "Yes — matches ACLU claim that ~2/3 of Americans live there"
  ),
  Source = c(
    "U.S. Census Bureau (2010–2020)",
    "ACLU",
    "ACLU, U.S. Census",
    "ACLU"
  )
)

kable(border_table, caption = "Quantifying the 100-Mile Border Zone")
```
```{r}
devtools::install_github("ropensci/rnaturalearthhires")

# Load required libraries
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(dplyr)
library(tidycensus)
library(ggplot2)
library(gghighlight)
library(ggrepel)
library(rnaturalearth)

# Set your Census API key
census_api_key("your_api_key_here")

# Step 1: Download U.S. City Population Data (simplemaps dataset)
city_data <- read.csv("data/uscities.csv")

# Step 2: Create a simple `sf` object for the cities
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(city_data, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# Step 3: Download U.S. Border Data (State Boundaries)
us_states <- ne_states(country = "United States of America", returnclass = "sf")

# Step 4: Create the 100-Mile Buffer Zone
buffer_dist <- 160934  # 100 miles in meters
us_states <- st_transform(us_states, crs = 5070)  # Transform to a projected CRS (equal area)
border_buffer <- st_buffer(us_states, dist = buffer_dist)

cities_sf <- st_transform(cities_sf, st_crs(border_buffer))

# Step 5: Filter Cities within the 100-Mile Buffer Zone
# Apply st_within() to get a logical matrix and convert it to a logical vector
cities_in_danger <- cities_sf %>%
  filter(apply(st_within(geometry, border_buffer, sparse = FALSE), 1, any))

# Check the result
print(cities_in_danger)

# Step 6: Get the 10 Most Populous Cities
top10_danger_cities <- cities_in_danger %>%
  arrange(desc(population)) %>%
  slice(1:10)

# Step 7: Create the Map
ggplot() +
  # Plot cities within the 100-mile border zone
  geom_sf(data = cities_in_danger, aes(color = population), size = 1) +
  
  # Highlight cities with color gradient from orange to darkred
  gghighlight(use_direct_label = FALSE) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred") +
  
  # Label the 10 most populous cities
  geom_label_repel(data = top10_danger_cities,
                   aes(geometry = geometry, label = city),
                   stat = "sf_coordinates",
                   size = 3,
                   max.overlaps = Inf) +
  
  # Additional map styling
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Most Populous Cities in the 100-Mile Border Zone",
       color = "Population") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Find the most populous city in each state within the Danger Zone
most_populous_by_state <- cities_in_danger %>%
  group_by(state_name) %>%
  filter(population == max(population)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Create the map
ggplot() +
  # Plot cities within the 100-mile border zone
  geom_sf(data = cities_in_danger, aes(color = population), size = 1) +
  
  # Highlight cities with a color gradient from orange to darkred
  gghighlight(use_direct_label = FALSE) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred") +
  
  # Label the most populous city in each state within the Danger Zone
  geom_label_repel(data = most_populous_by_state,
                   aes(geometry = geometry, label = city),
                   stat = "sf_coordinates",
                   size = 3,
                   max.overlaps = Inf) +
  
  # Additional map styling
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Most Populous Cities in Each State within the 100-Mile Border Zone",
       color = "Population") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```
